title: Acceptance probability invariance
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on a Boolean input $x$, and let $C$ and $D$ be configurations on that input. If their states, input-head positions, work-tape contents, and work-tape head positions agree, and their output lists have the same summary (empty, exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$, or unable ever to become $[\mathrm{true}]$ by appending symbols), then for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$ the probability that a uniformly random length-$j$ choice word leads from $C$ to a halted configuration with output exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ equals the corresponding probability from $D$.
hypotheses_covered: C and D are configurations of N on x
Their core data and output summaries agree
